newsitem.title: USA: Carso unit sees sales up 10 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Carso unit sees sales up 10 pct in 1996.

text.p: Carso Industrial, a unit of Mexican conglomerate Grupo Carso, likely will see an increase of more than 10 percent in sales this year, a senior executive said on Wednesday.
"We have had an increase of 11 percent for the first nine months (of 1996) and the trend should continue," Fernando Chico Pardo, a company partner and director, told Reuters,
Chico Pardo, who spoke at a Bear Stearns investor conference, said 1995 net sales were 21.5 billion pesos. The company reported 1996 nine-month sales of 16.4 billion pesos.
He said net income for the first three quarters of 1996 was 2.4 billion pesos, down from 2.8 billion a year earlier. Total 1995 income was 2.7 billion pesos.
Sales at the company's Cigatam tobacco unit, one of the biggest of Carso's six main units, fell seven percent in the first nine months of 1996 from a year ago, to 3.6 billion pesos.
The fall was offset in part by an increase of 13.2 percent at Condumex, a cable and auto parts unit, to 4.2 billion pesos.
Grupo Carso is the single biggest shareholder of Telefonos de Mexico, and Chico Pardo said Carso was on schedule to increase its stake from 10 percent now to 17.3 percent by October 1999.
Asked by analysts about when Carso might stop buying Telmex stock, he said, "I don't have any concern about the price of the stock. Do we have a target price for the stock? No."
